title: DGFiP's “Foncier innovant” deep-learning detection of undeclared swimming pools: 20,000+ pools taxed for 2022, about €10 million for communes
summary: DGFiP deep-learning pool detection: 20,000+ pools taxed for 2022 (~€10m for communes); 150,000 taxable pools found across metropolitan France excluding Paris and overseas departments
account: France's Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) runs “Foncier innovant”. A deep-learning algorithm finds building and pool outlines in public IGN aerial images. An automated check compares them to land-tax files. A tax agent verifies every anomaly before the owner is contacted. DGFiP's October 2021 note says Capgemini provided project-management and build assistance and Google the cloud infrastructure and services for developing the AI models. The 2022 experiment in nine departments led to more than 20,000 pools being taxed for 2022. That was close to €10 million of extra revenue for the communes concerned (DGFiP, 2 June 2023). The sources do not date the result separately from the announcement. The Sénat's April 2024 report puts the cost at €24 million. After generalization in 2023, the first pass covered metropolitan France, excluding Paris and the overseas departments (DROM). It detected 150,000 untaxed taxable pools, which the Sénat report calls “potentiellement taxables”. Industrialization began in June 2024.
purpose: Detect undeclared pools and buildings from aerial imagery to bring them into the local property-tax base
system: Foncier innovant (DGFiP): open-source deep-learning segmentation of IGN orthophotos cross-checked with cadastral and tax files
developer: DGFiP (Délégation à la transformation numérique) with Capgemini (assistance à maîtrise d'ouvrage et maîtrise d'œuvre) and Google (cloud infrastructure and AI-model development services)
domain: Tax administration: local property tax base
taxonomy_note: The realized good is about 10 million euros in extra tax revenue for communes, which no type names, and the type names the detection of undeclared pools from aerial images.

ratings.reason: Aggregate program results; no discrete attributable event.
Revenue totals for communes (about €10 million for 2022) are program aggregates.
National program figures (150,000 pools detected) without a discrete event.

ai_role.statement: Official sources describe the chain (AI detection, automated file check, human verification, owner contact) and attribute the taxed pools to it. No evaluation isolates the algorithm's contribution from the human verification and declaration campaign. The Assemblée nationale written answer of 14 December 2021 confirms DGFiP's use of AI on IGN imagery and that contractors do not access tax data.

headline: DGFiP's Foncier innovant leads to 20,000+ pools taxed for 2022
metric: more than 20,000 pools being taxed for 2022, close to €10 million of extra revenue

later.note: The Sénat's April 2024 report records the generalization to all of metropolitan France in 2023, for about 150,000 potentially taxable pools, and the DGCL page dates an industrialization phase from June 2024.
later.quote: Le dispositif a donc été généralisé en 2023 à l’ensemble de la métropole (la Corse et l’Outre-mer devraient suivre), pour environ 150 000 piscines potentiellement taxables au total, soit une part non négligeable (5 %) des 3 millions de piscines enterrées que compte la France.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the cited sources.
Paired with AI Incident Database incident 1082 (medium confidence); severity not given by the source.

Limited the 150,000-pool figure to metropolitan France excluding Paris and the overseas departments as the DGCL page does and added the Sénat's “potentiellement taxables” wording; stated that the date observed is the publication date of the DGFiP announcement; credited Google with AI-model development services as well as cloud infrastructure per the DGFiP note; restored the page title “Expérimentation du Foncier innovant” on the 2021 evidence item; and re-dated the generalization echo to May 2023 (month only) with e-mails rather than letters as the DGFiP describes.
Added what happened since from the cited sources.
Benefit type set to Improved Knowledge Discovery under Trustible's full taxonomy of 23 types; it was Improved Organizational Efficiency among the six first used.
Country of the developer and the deployer added from the organization's own site or a registry.
Prose pass: account, the system's part rewritten in shorter sentences with abbreviations expanded; facts, figures and quotations unchanged.
